description:
Verifies a cold start could actually catch up from what is in object storage.

Checks:
- The latest s/{tag}/ bundle per shard has a valid index record (magic 0x4F4C5644, 16-byte header, trailing payload_size footer). Validate via SnapshotBundle.find_index_boundary/1 rather than reimplementing the framing.
- The bundle's embedded durable_version is <= that shard's max chunk version.
- Chunks covering [snapshot_version, ...] forward still exist. If they do not, cold start cannot catch up -- a silent, latent unrecoverability that nothing surfaces until a node actually restarts.

Unlike chunks, snapshots ARE pruned (Snapshot.delete_older_than/2), so the pruning boundary is a live correctness concern rather than a no-op.

Known limitation to document rather than solve: durable version is not persisted to object storage -- it is RAM-only in ShardServer and aggregated by Demux.Durability.min_durable_version/1. fsck can derive max-chunk-version but cannot independently verify the cluster's own durability claim. Worth stating plainly in the task output so nobody reads more assurance into a green run than it provides.
title: fsck: snapshot and chunk continuity
